The segmentation of nanoscale electron microscopy (MR) images is important but
challenging in connectomics. Recent developments in deep learning have shown
the enormous possibility of automatic segmentation for tera-scale EM images.
Unfortunately, none of the existing segmentation techniques are error-free, and they
involve proofreading, which is usually implemented as an interactive,
semi-automatic procedure through manual intervention. Herein, we propose a completely
automatic proofreading approach based on reinforcement learning. The primary concept is
to model the human decision process in proofreading using a reinforcement agent
to achieve fully automatic proofreading. We systematically design the proposed
system by using several reinforcement learning agents in a hierarchical
way, where each agency relies only on a particular task while maintaining
dependency between agents. However, we also show that the episodic
task setting of reinforcement learning can effectively handle a combination of
split and split errors concurrently presented in the input. We demonstrate the
effectiveness of the proposed system by using it with state-of-the-art
proofreading techniques using different testing examples.

While deep convolutional neural systems achieved remarkable progress in
medical image computing and research, its paradigm of supervised learning
demands a huge number of annotations for training to reduce overfitting and
achieving promising outcomes. In scientific practices, large semantic
annotations are easy to obtain in some circumstances where specialized
biomedical expert expertise is needed, and it is not a common condition
where only few annotated classes are available. In this work, we proposed a
novel technique for few-shot medical picture segmentation, which allows a
segmentation model to fast generalize to an unseen class with few training
images. We construct our few-shot image segmentor using a deep convolutional
network trained episodically. Motivated by the temporal accuracy and
consistency in medical images, we developed an efficient global correlation
module to capture the similarity between a support and query image and
incorporate it into the deep network called global correlation network.
Specifically, we enhance discriminability of deep embedding to encourage clustering
of the feature domains of the same class while keep the feature domains of
multiple organs farther away. Ablation Study showed the validity of the
proposed global correlation module and discriminative embedding loss. Numerous
studies on anatomical abdomen images on both CT and MRI techniques are
performed to establish the state-of-the-art efficiency of our proposed
model.

even if convolutional neural connections (CNNs) are driving progress in
medical image segmentation, standard models now have some limitations. Second,
the use of multi-scale techniques, i.e., encoder-decoder interfaces, leads
to a redundant use of information, where different low-level features are
extracted many times at different scales. Second, long-range feature
dependencies are not easily modeled, resulting in non-optimal
discriminative feature representations correlated with each semantic class. In
this paper we attempt to resolve these difficulties with the proposed
architecture, by creating richer semantic dependencies based on the use of
guided self-attention mechanisms. This technique is able to integrate regional
features with their corresponding regional dependencies, as well as highlight
interdependent channel maps in an adaptive way. Further, the additional loss
between multiple components guides the attention mechanisms to neglect irrelevant
data and focus on more discriminant areas of the image by recognizing
specific feature associations. We evaluate the proposed model in the context of
semantic segmentation on four different datasets: abdominal organs,
cardiac systems and brain cells. A series of ablation studies
support the importance of these attention components in the proposed design.
In addition, compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation systems our simulation
yields greater segmentation efficiency, improving the precision of the
predictions while lowering the standard variance. This shows the
effectiveness of our method to produce accurate and efficient automatic
segmentations of medical images. Our code is made publicly accessible at
http://github.com/sinAshish/Multi-Scale-Attention

Picture segmentation is one of the most important functions of computer vision.
In certain practical systems, it is necessary to carefully improve the
validity of individual segmentation results. In this study, we propose a
novel methodology to provide the empirical significance of segmentation findings
in the form of p-values. Additionally, we consider a quantitative hypothesis
test for measuring the difference between the object and the background
regions. This problem is challenging because the difference can be fairly
small (called segmentation bias) due to the adaptation of the segmentation
algorithm to the database. To resolve this obstacle, we introduce a mathematical
technique termed selective inference, and establish a methodology to compute valid
p-values in which the segmentation bias is fully accounted for. Since the
proposed structure is potentially relevant to many segmentation
algorithms, we focus in this paper on graph cut-based and threshold-based
segmentation algorithm, and identify three specific techniques to compute valid
p-values for the segmentation results provided by these algorithms. We prove
the mathematical validity of these three techniques and establish their
practicality by using them to segmentation solutions for medical images.

Registration is a key task in scientific imagery research which can be
applied to many functions including image segmentation, intra-operative
monitoring, multi-modal image alignment, and motion prediction. Popular
registration methods such as ANTs and NiftyReg optimize an objective function for
each pair of pictures from scratch which is time-consuming for small pictures with
complex deformation. Facilitated by the slow progress of deep learning,
learning-based methods such as VoxelMorph have been developing for image
registration. These methods can reach competitive efficiency in a
fraction of a third on advanced GPUs. In this work, we construct a neural
registration framework, called NeurReg, with a hybrid loss of displacement
fields and data similarity, which greatly improves the current
state-of-the-art of registrations. Within the implementation, we simulate various
transformations by a registration simulator which provides fixed image and
displacement field ground truth for training. Additionally, we design two
segmentation frameworks based on the proposed registration framework: 1)
atlas-based segmentation, 2) joint learning of both segmentation and
registration tasks, and 3) multi-task learning with atlas-based segmentation as
an intermediate feature. Numerous experimental findings validate the
validity of the proposed NeurReg framework based on several indicators: the
endpoint error (EPE) of the predicted displacement field, mean square error
(MSE), normalized local cross-correlation (NLCC), mutual information (IL), Dice
coefficient, uncertainty analysis, and the interpretability of the
segmentation. The proposed NeurReg increases registration accuracy with fast
inference speed, which can significantly accelerate related medical image analysis
activities.

Spleen volume analysis using automated image segmentation method can be
applied to identify splenomegaly (abnormally expanded liver) on Magnetic Resonance
Imaging (MRI) scans. In recent times, Deep Convolutional Brain Network (DCNN)
segmentation techniques have shown benefits for abdominal organ
segmentation. Moreover, alterations in both length and size of the spleen on MRI
images can result in significant true positive and true negative labeling when
deploying DCNN based approaches. In this paper, we propose the Splenomegaly
Segmentation Networks (SSNet) to address temporal differences when analyzing
very small spleens. SSNet was created based on the methodology of
image-to-image conditional generative adversarial networks (cGAN).
Additionally, the Global Convolutional Networks (GCN) was designed as the generator
to eliminate false negatives, while the Markovian discriminator (PatchGAN) was
designed to reduce false positives. A study of clinically acquired 3D MRI scans
(both T1 weighted and T2 weighted) from patients with splenomegaly were employed to
train and test the networks. The experimental results showed that a mean
Dice coefficient of 0.9260 and a average Dice coefficient of 0.9262 using SSNet
on independently examined MRI volumes of patients with splenomegaly.

In this work we address the task of semantic image segmentation with Deep
Learning and make two major contributions that are experimentally shown to
have considerable theoretical merit. First, we highlight convolution with
upsampled filters, or 'atrous convolution', as a powerful tool in dense
prediction tasks. Atrous convolution enables you to explicitly control the
resolution at which feature responses are measured within Deep Convolutional
Neural Network. It additionally requires you to quickly enlarge the field of view of
filters to incorporate larger context without reducing the number of
variables or the amount of computation. Second, we propose atrous spatial
pyramid pooling (ASPP) to robustly segment objects at different scales. ASPP
probes an incoming convolutional feature layer with filters at different
sampling rates and effective fields-of-views, thereby capturing objects as well as
image context at different scales. First, we improve the localization of object
boundaries by using techniques from DCNNs and probabilistic graphical models.
The widely implemented combination of max-pooling and downsampling in DCNNs
achieves invariance but has a toll on localization accuracy. We overcome this
by merging the responses at the initial DCNN layer with a partially connected
Conditional Random Field (CRF), which is shown both qualitatively and
systematically to reduce localization efficiency. Our proposed "DeepLab"
system sets the new state-of-art at the PASCAL VOC-2012 semantic image
segmentation task, reaching 79.7% mIOU in the test set, and advances the
results on four other datasets: PASCAL-Context, PASCAL-Person-Part, and
Cityscapes. All of our code is made publicly accessible online.

We present the second approach to handle curvature regularity in region-based
image segmentation and inpainting that is independent of initialization.
  To this end we start from a new formulation of length-based optimization
schemes, based on surface continuation constraints, and consider the connections
to existing schemes. The formulation is based on a \emph{cell complex} and
uses basic states and boundary elements. The corresponding optimization
solution is cast as an integer linear program.
  We then show how the method can be extended to include curvature regularity,
again cast as an integer linear program. Here, we are comparing pairs of
boundary elements to reflect curvature. Similarly, a constraint set is generated
to determine that the boundary variables actually reflect the boundary of the
regions defined by the region parameters.
  We show that by solving the linear programming relaxation one comes very
close to the global optimum, and that curvature regularity is therefore much
more suited in the absence of long and thin objects compared to standard
length regularity.

In the current paper, electrical transport properties of 25 nm thin Nb films
sputtered on the photosensitive substrate BiOCl were investigated in the
heat range 7.5 C $\leq T \leq$ 8.5 K. The impact of blue (532 nm)
and blue (640 nm) laser excitations on resistive superconducting transitions of
the copper thin films on a polymer crystal and BiOCl double crystal surfaces
were studied. The temperature dependences of the resistivity for Nb are in strong
agreement with the McMillan model which shows the strong impact of the
inverse proximity effect induced by the interface. The increased influence of
the BiOCl/Nb interface under laser stimulation refers to the lowering the
ratio of the density of normal to superconductivity carriers in the
$T\rightarrow 0$ limit and this observation is in cooperation with the
photoconductivity study of BiOCl single crystals.

We set up an algebraic structure for the analysis of pseudoholomorphic discs
bounding nonorientable Lagrangians, as well as equivariant extensions of such
complexes resulting from a torus action.
  Next, we define unital cyclic twisted $A_\infty$ algebras and prove some
fundamental findings about them, including a homological perturbation theorem which
enables one to build minimal models of such algebras. We then construct an
equivariant extension of $A_\infty$ algebras which are invariant under a torus
action on the underlying complex. Then, we construct a homotopy retraction
of the Cartan-Weil complex to equivariant algebra, which enables we to
build minimal models for equivariant cyclic twisted $A_\infty$ algebras.
  In a upcoming paper we will use these results to identify and obtain
fixed-point expressions for the open Gromov-Witten theory of $\mathbb{CP}^{2n}
\hookrightarrow \mathbb{SP}^{2n}$, as well as its equivariant extension.

A double-helix electrode configuration is combined with a $^{10}$B powder
coating method to develop large-area (9 in $\times$ 36 in) neutron sensors.
The nuclear detector performance for each of the three prototypes is equivalent
to a single 2-bar $^3$He drift tube of the same diameter (36 in). One unit has
been operational continuously for 18 years and the change of efficiency is
greater than 1%. An empirical model for pulse heigh spectra is presented and the
predicted mean film length agrees with the experiment to within 30%. Further
sensor optimization is possible through film texture, power size, moderator
box and gas. The estimated manufacturing price per unit is greater than 3k US\$ and
the technology is thus ideal for deployment in small numbers.

In this paper, we investigate an optimal boundary control solution for a three
dimensional simplified Ericksen--Gordon system modelling the incompressible
nematic fluid crystal flows. The hydrodynamic system consists of the
Navier--Maxwell equations for the flow speed coupled with a convective
Ginzburg--Klein type formula for the averaged molecular orientation. The
fluid speed is considered to satisfy a no-slip boundary condition, while the
molecular orientation is subject to a time-dependent Dirichlet boundary
condition that corresponds to the strong anchoring condition for liquid
crystals. We first establish the existence of optimal boundary controls. Then
we show that the control-to-state operator is Fr\'echet differentiable between
appropriate Banach spaces and derive first-order necessary equilibrium
terms in terms of a variational inequality involving the adjoint state
variables.

We prove that the moduli space of invariant G_2-metrics on a closed 7-manifold
is in general disconnected by introducing a number of explicit examples.
  We detect other connected parts of the G_2-moduli space by defining
an integer-valued analytic refinement of the nu-invariant, a Z/48-valued defect
invariant of G_2-structures on a closed 7-manifold introduced by the second and
second researchers. The refined theorem is defined using eta invariants and
Mathai-Quillen currents on the 7-manifold and we compute it for twisted
connected sums \`a la Kovalev, Corti-Haskins-Nordstr\"om-Pacini and
extra-twisted connected sums as constructed by the third and fourth authors. In
particular, we find instances of G_2-holonomy metrics in certain parts of
the moduli space where the associated G_2-structures are symmetric and other
instances where they are not.

A polynomial skew product of C^2 is a map of the form p(z,w) = (r(z),
q(z,w)), where p and q are integers, such that z is regular of degree d >=
2. For algebraic maps of R, hyperbolicity is analogous to the condition that
the closure of the postcritical set is disjoint from the Julia set; further,
critical points either iterate to an attracting cycle or infinity. For
polynomial skew products, Jensen (Math. Ann., 1999) established that f is
Axiom A if and only if the closure of the postcritical set is disjoint from the
right analog of the Julia set. Here we present the analogous conclusion:
critical orbits either escape to infinity or accumulate on an attracting set.
In addition, we construct new instances of Axiom A maps demonstrating different
postcritical behaviors.

The inability to identify change-points in a dynamic network or a time series of
graphs is an extremely difficult task in various applications of the emerging
discipline of graph signal processing. This paper examines change-point
detection as a hypothesis testing problem in terms of a generative latent
position model, relying on the special case of the Stochastic Block Model time
series. We analyze three classes of scan statistics, based on distinct underlying
locality data described in the study. Our primary contribution is the
derivation of the limiting distributions and power characteristics of the
competing scan statistics. Performance is compared theoretically, on synthetic
statistics, and on the Enron email corpus. We demonstrate that both data are
admissible in one simple set, while one of the data is inadmissible a
single setting.

The intention of this paper to draw attention to different issues of the algebraic
dependence in algebras. The topic begins with discussions of the algebraic
dependence problem in polynomial algebras. Then the Burchnall-Chaundy
construction for finding algebraic dependence and applying the corresponding
algebraic curves for commuting differential operators in the Heisenberg theorem
is published. Next some old and new findings on algebraic dependence of commuting
q-difference operators and elements in q-deformed Heisenberg algebras are
published. The main ideas and essence of three proofs of this are examined and
compared. One is the algorithmic dimension growth existence proof. The other is
the recent proof extending the Burchnall-Chaundy approach from differential
operators and the Heisenberg theorem to the q-deformed Einstein algebra,
demonstrating that the Burchnall-Chaundy eliminant construction actually gives
annihilating curves for commuting elements in the q-deformed Heisenberg
algebras for p not a root of unity.

Deep learning-based segmentation techniques are sensitive to unexpected data
distribution changes during deployment, e.g. change of picture appearances or
contrasts caused by multiple scanners, unexpected imaging artifacts etc. In
this paper, we present a cooperative methodology for training image segmentation
models and a latent space augmentation approach for producing hard examples.
Both contributions improve model generalization and effectiveness with limited
data. The collaborative training methodology consists of a fast-thinking network
(FTN) and a slow-thinking network (STN). The FTN develops decoupled image
features and shape features for image reconstruction and segmentation tasks.
The STN teaches shape priors for segmentation correction and refinement. The three
systems are trained in a collaborative way. The latent space augmentation
provides challenging examples for training by masking the decoupled latent
space in both channel-wise and spatial-wise manners. We performed numerous
studies on public cardiac imaging data. Using only 10 subjects from a
single site for training, we demonstrated improved cross-site segmentation
efficiency and improved sensitivity against other unforeseen imaging
artifacts compared to strong baseline techniques. Also, cooperative
training with latent space data augmentation yields 15% improvement in terms of
average Dice score when compared to a standardized training procedure.

Clinical image segmentation is one of the fundamental functions of computer-aided
diagnosis in clinical imagery research. While most clinical images have the
characteristics of blurred boundaries and irregular intensity distribution,
through existing segmentation techniques, the discontinuity within the target region
and the discontinuity of the target boundary are unlikely to lead to rough or
possibly erroneous boundary delineation. In this paper, we propose a new iterative
refined interactive segmentation approach for medical images Based on agent
reinforcement learning, which relies on the problem of target segmentation
boundaries. We model the dynamic procedure of drawing the target contour in a
particular order as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) Based on a deep reinforcement
learning approach. In the dynamic process of continuous communication between the
agent and the image, the agent tracks the boundary point by point in order
within a limited length range until the contour of the target is fully
drawn. In this process, the agent can easily evaluate the segmentation
efficiency by exploring an interactive policy in the image. The approach we
proposed is quick and efficient. At the same time, we evaluate our methodology on
the cardiac MRI scan data set. Experimental findings show that our technique has a
greater segmentation effect on the left ventricle in a large number of medical
image data sets, especially in terms of segmentation boundaries, this technique is
cheaper than existing techniques. Based on our proposed technique, the dynamic
generation process of the predicted contour path of the left ventricle
will be shown online at http://github.com/H1997ym/LV-contour-trajectory.

Semantic image segmentation seeks to provide object labels with precise
boundaries, which often suffers from overfitting. Recently, other data
augmentation methods like regional dropout and mix strategies have been
proposed to address the issue. These methods have demonstrated to be beneficial
for guiding the model to attend on less discriminative parts. Moreover, current
methods operate at the image level, and objects and the background are
coupled. However, the boundaries are not properly augmented due to the fixed semantic
scenario. In this paper, we propose ObjectAug to perform object-level
augmentation for semantic image segmentation. ObjectAug first decouples the
imagery into individual items and the background using the semantic labels.
Next, each object is augmented separately with widely used augmentation
techniques (e.g., scaling, shifting, and rotation). Then, the gray area brought
by object augmentation is further restored using image inpainting. Then, the
augmented objects and background are assembled as an augmented picture. In this
manner, the boundaries can be thoroughly explored in the different conceptual scenarios. In
addition, ObjectAug can provide category-aware augmentation that provides multiple
possibilities to objects in each category, and can be quickly combined with
existing image-level augmentation procedures to further enhance efficiency.
Comprehensive studies are conducted on both natural image and medical imagery
data. Experiment results show that our ObjectAug can also
reduce segmentation efficiency.

The importance of hierarchical image organization has been witnessed by a
broad spectrum of applications in computer vision and graphics. Different from
picture segmentation with the spatial whole-part consideration, this work designs
a modern methodology for disassembling an image into a family of derived signals
from a scale-space approach. Moreover, we first offer a formal
definition of image disassembly. Then, by concerning desired properties, such
as peeling hierarchy and structure preservation, we convert the original
complex solution into a series of two-component separation sub-problems,
greatly increasing the complexity. The proposed implementation is robust to
both supervised and unsupervised settings. A compact recurrent network, namely
hierarchical image peeling net, is customized to easily and efficiently
fulfill the task, which is about 3.5Mb in length, and can handle 1080p images in
more than 60 fps per recurrence on a GTX 2080Ti CPU, making it ideal for
practical usage. Both empirical results and theoretical findings are provided
to prove the effectiveness of the proposed framework, reveal its superiority
over other state-of-the-art alternatives, and show its potential to various
applicable scenarios. Our code is accessible at
\url{https://github.com/ForawardStar/HIPe}.

Over the last few decades, state-of-the-art image segmentation algorithms are
based on deep convolutional neural connections. To render a deep network with the
capability to comprehend a design, humans have to collect a small quantity of
pixel-level annotated data to train the models, which is time-consuming and
costly. Recently, few-shot segmentation is proposed to resolve this issue.
Few-shot segmentation aims to develop a segmentation model that can be
generalized to novel classes with only a few training images. In this paper, we
propose a cross-reference network (CRNet) for few-shot segmentation. Like
current works which only predict the mask in the query image, our proposed
model concurrently make assumptions for both the support image and the search
image. With a cross-reference mechanism, our network can better identify the
co-occurrent objects in the two images, thereby enabling the few-shot segmentation
task. We therefore develop a mask refinement module to recurrently refine the
prediction of the foreground regions. For the $k$-shot learning, we propose to
finetune parts of networks to take advantage of multiple labeled support
images. Experiments on the PASCAL VOC 2012 database demonstrate that our network
promotes state-of-the-art efficiency.

instead of directly using an observed image including some outliers,
noise or intensity inhomogeneity, the use of its ideal value (e.g. noise-free
image) has a positive effect on clustering. Furthermore, the accurate measurement of
the residual (e.g. unknown noise) between the observed image and its ideal
value is an difficult task. To do so, we propose an $\ell_0$
regularization-based Fuzzy $C$-Means (FCM) algorithm using a
morphological reconstruction operation and a tight wavelet frame transform. To
obtain a sound trade-off between detail restoration and noise suppression,
morphological reconstruction is designed to filter an observed picture. By merging
the observed and filtered pictures, a weighted sum picture is created. Because a
tight wavelet frame system has sparse representations of an image, it is
employed to decompose the weighted sum picture, thereby creating its corresponding
feature set. Taking it as data for clustering, we present an improved FCM
algorithm by imposing an $\ell_0$ regularization term on the residual between
the feature set and its ideal value, which means that the favorable
approximation of the residual is obtained and the optimal value participates in
clustering. Spatial data is often introduced into clustering because it is
naturally encountered in image segmentation. Also, it makes the
analysis of the residual more efficient. To further reduce the segmentation
effects of the improved FCM algorithms, we also employ the morphological
reconstruction to smoothen the labels produced by clustering. Then, based
on the prototypes and smoothed labels, the segmented image is transformed by
applying a tight wavelet frame reconstruction operation. Experimental findings
reported for synthetic, medical, and color images show that the proposed
algorithms is efficient and reliable, and outperforms other algorithms.

This work describes the use of statistical approximations of uncertainty from
deep learning in a robot planner, demonstrating that this creates more risky
decisions in safety-critical situations. The case study investigated is inspired
by a setup where an airborne robot acts as a "scout" for a ground robot. This is
important when the below area is uncertain or hazardous, with applications in space
exploration, military, or search-and-rescue. Pictures taken from the aerial perspective
are designed to obtain a less obstructed map to guide the navigation of the robot
on the ground. Experiments are conducted employing a deep learning semantic image
segmentation, followed by a path planner based on the resulting cost map, to
give an analytical evaluation of the proposed approach. A comparison with different
methods is presented to portray the effectiveness of different methods, or
differences within a method, in different theoretical settings. The technique is
analyzed to identify the effect of differences in the uncertainty extraction, as
well as the presence of an uncertainty metric, on the overall system with the
use of a defined metric which measures surprise to the planner. The assessment is
done on different datasets, indicating a similar trend of lower surprise when
uncertainty information is incorporated in the planning, given threshold values
of the parameters in the uncertainty extraction have been met. We find
that taking uncertainty into account leads to paths that may be 18% more
expensive on an average.

Segmentation of colorectal cancerous areas from 3D Magnetic Resonance (MR)
images is a crucial process for cancer which typically requires
precise delineation of tumour boundaries at an cost of labor, time and
reproducibility. While deep learning based techniques serve good baselines in 3D
image segmentation tasks, small applicable patch length limits effective
receptive field and degrades segmentation efficiency. In addition, Regions of
interest (RoIs) localization from small whole volume 3D images serves as a
preceding operation that brings about many advantages in terms of speed,
target accuracy, elimination of false positives. Distinct from sliding window
or non-joint localization-segmentation based models, we propose a novel
multitask structure referred to as 3D RoI-aware U-Net (3D RU-Net), for RoI
localization and in-region segmentation where the three tasks share one backbone
encoder network. With the region proposals from the encoder, we crop
multi-level RoI in-region features from the encoder to form a GPU
memory-efficient decoder for detailpreserving segmentation and thus
enlarged applicable volume length and effective receptive field. To efficiently
train the model, we designed a Dice formulated loss function for the
global-to-local multi-task learning process. Based on the performance gains,
we went on to ensemble models with many receptive fields to obtain far
greater efficiency costing minor additional computational expensiveness. Extensive
studies were conducted on 64 cancerous cases with a four-fold
cross-validation, and the findings had considerable superiority in terms of
reliability and reliability over traditional frameworks. In conclusion, the
proposed approach has a significant impact for extension to other 3D object
segmentation functions from medical images due to its inherent generalizability.
The code for the proposed approach is publicly accessible.

Weakly-supervised image segmentation is an essential task in computer vision.
A fundamental issue is how to obtain low quality objects location from image-level
category. Classification activation mapping is a common technique which can be
applied to produce high-precise object location cues. Unfortunately these location cues
are often very sparse and large such that they can not give effective
information for picture segmentation. In this paper, we propose a saliency guided
image segmentation network to solve this issue. We employ a self-attention
saliency approach to produce subtle saliency maps, and render the location cues
grow as seeds by seeded region growing technique to expand pixel-level labels
extent. In the process of seeds growing, we use the saliency values to weight
the similarity between pixels to control the growing. Thus saliency
information can help create discriminative object regions, and the effects
of wrong salient pixels can be suppressed easily. Experimental findings on
a common segmentation dataset PASCAL VOC2012 demonstrate the validity of
our technique.

This manuscript discusses the problem of prominent object detection and
recognition inspired by the notion that human seems to priorities perception of
scene elements. The problem deals with identifying the most relevant area of
interest, segmenting the specific item/object in that region, and assigning it an
object class label. In other words, we are solving the four issues of
saliency modeling, saliency detection, and object recognition under one
umbrella. The motive behind such a problem formulation is (1) the benefits
to the knowledge representation-based vision pipelines, and (2) the potential
improvements in emulating bio-inspired vision technologies by solving these two
issues separately. We are foreseeing expanding this problem formulation to
fully semantically segmented scenes with instance object priority for
high-level inferences in many applications including assistive vision. Along
with a new problem definition, we also suggest a methodology to achieve such a task.
The proposed model predicts the most significant area in the image, segments the
associated items, and labels them. The proposed problem and method are
evaluated against human fixations, annotated segmentation masks, and object
class categories. We define a chance level for each of the evaluation criterion
to compare the proposed algorithm with. With the poor reliability of the
proposed baseline, the overall analyses indicate that the issue of
prominent object detection and recognition is a challenging task that is not
worth exploring further.

Paleness or pallor is a manifestation of blood loss or high oxygen
levels in the human blood that can be triggered by diseases such as
disease. This work provides the first automated screening system that provides
pallor site images, segments, and extracts color and intensity-based features
for multi-class classification of patients with low pallor due to anemia-like
diseases, normal patients and patients with other disorders. This work
uses the pallor sites of conjunctiva and tongue for anemia screening
purposes. Second, for the eye pallor site images, the sclera and conjunctiva
areas are automatically segmented for areas of interest. However, for the
tongue pallor site images, the inner and outer cheek areas are segmented.
Then, color-plane based feature processing is performed followed by machine
learning algorithm for feature reduction and image level classification for
anemia. In this work, a suite of classification algorithms image-level
classifications for normal (class 0), pallor (class 1) and other abnormalities
(class 2). The proposed technique achieves 86% precision, 85% accuracy and 67%
recall in eye pallor site images and 98.2% precision and accuracy with 100%
recall in tongue pallor site images for classification of images with pallor.
The proposed pallor screening system can be further fine-tuned to identify the
prevalence of anemia-like diseases using controlled set of local images that
can then be applied for future analysis purposes.

Contour detection has been a crucial element in various image segmentation
and object detection applications. Most recent work utilized low-level features
such as color or saliency to identify shapes and then utilize them as cues for a
higher-level task such as object detection. Instead, we claim that identifying
objects and predicting contours are three mutually related functions. Contrary to
conventional methods, we show that we can invert the commonly recognized
pipeline: Instead of identifying contours with low-level cues for a higher-level
recognition task, we exploit object-related features as high-level cues for
contour detection.
  We achieve this goal by means of a multi-scale deep network that consists of
four convolutional layers and a bifurcated fully-connected sub-network. The
section from the input layer to the second convolutional layer is fixed and
directly lifted from a pre-trained network optimized over a large-scale object
classification task. This section of the network is applied to three distinct
scales of the image input. These two concurrent and different streams are then
attached to a bifurcated sub-network consisting of four independently-trained
branches. one branch tries to predict the contour likelihood (with a
classification objective) while the other branch is trained to find the
fraction of human labelers agreeing about the contour presence at a given moment
(with a regression criterion).
  We show that without any feature engineering our multi-scale deep learning
method produces state-of-the-art results in contour detection.

In this paper we present a general problem for multi-target tracking with
superpositional measurements. Measurements that are functions of the sum of the
contributions of the targets present in the surveillance area are called
superpositional measurements. We base our modelling on Labeled Random Finite
Set (RFS) in order to independently estimate the number of targets and their
trajectories. This modelling leads to a labeled version of Mahler's
multi-target Bayes filter. Unfortunately, a simple development of this
tracker using Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) techniques is not possible due to the
limitations of sampling in low dimensional spaces. We propose an optimal
multi-target sampling approach based on Superpositional Approximate CPHD
(SA-CPHD) filter and the newly introduced Labeled Multi-Bernoulli (LMB) and
Vo-Vo densities. The effectiveness of the proposed technique is verified through
simulation in a challenging radar application with carefully spaced objectives and
high signal-to-noise ratio.

We investigate the ultrafast optical properties of single
Al0.3Ga0.7As/GaAs-core-shell-nanowires. The nanowires include GaAs-based
quantum wells. For a resonant excitation of the quantum wells, we find a
picosecond voltage which is consistent with an ultrafast lateral expansion
of the photogenerated charge carriers. This Dember-effect does not occur for an
excitation of the GaAs-based core of the nanowires. However, the core exhibits
an ultrafast displacement current and a photo-thermoelectric current at the
metal Schottky contacts. Our findings uncover the optoelectronic interactions in
silicon core-shell nanowires containing quantum wells, and they
show the idea to use the low-dimensional quantum well states
therein for ultrafast molecules and sensors.

With the continuous growth of web applications, social networks, and
other relevant sectors, user authentication gets more and more necessary to
protect the data of users. Password encryption is one of the commonly employed
techniques to obtain encryption for legal users and defence against
attackers. There have been several password-cracking techniques introduced during the
last decades, and people have been developing countermeasures against password
breaking all the time. Unfortunately, we find that the survey work on password
breaking research has not been completed very well. This paper is mainly to provide a
detailed evaluation of the encryption cracking techniques, import methods of encryption
cracking, and the countermeasures against password cracking that are typically
used at three phases including the password design phase (e.g. user
education, dynamic encryption, usage of tokens, computer generations) and after the
design (e.g. reactive password check, proactive password checking, encryption
security, access control). The primary aim of this work is to provide the
abecedarian IT protection experts and the common audiences some knowledge
about software encryption and encryption cracking and promote the growth of
this area. Keywords- Software encryption; User encryption; Password cracking;
Cryptanalysis; Countermeasures

Text data is generally viewed as "take-away" materials with little noise and difficult
to process data. Main concerns are how to take data and transform them
into a good document format. But data can be susceptible to noise often called
errors. Ambiguities are understood from a short period, especially because polysemy is
obvious in grammar and context is required to eliminate confusion. I claim in
this paper that linguistic context is not suffisant to improve interpretation.
In this paper I try to say that firstly noise can emerge from natural data
themselves, not involving high technology, secondly texts, seen as verified
but irrelevant, can spoil content of a corpus; it can lead to contradictions
and background noise.

We present a coarse-graining approach that we test for aqueous mixtures. The
method provides pair-wise cumulative coordination as a target function within an
iterative Boltzmann inversion (IBI) like protocol. We name this method
coordination iterative Boltzmann inversion ($\mathcal {M}-$IBI). While the
underlying coarse-grained model is not structure based and, therefore, preserves
pair-wise solution structure, our approach only reproduces solvation
thermodynamics of binary and/or binary mixtures. However, we observe much
better convergence within $\mathcal {F}-$IBI compared to IBI. To prove the
robustness, we apply $\mathcal {B}-$IBI to study test cases of solvation
thermodynamics of acidic urea and a triglycine solvation in acidic urea.

based on elastic collisions, the linear momentum of a slow electron can be
determined from as few as three successive recoil electron tracks plus the vertex
position of the first collision, or `one and half' ion tracks. If the time
delay between the next three successive ion tracks is not measured, the number
of ion tracks can be shortened to two and a quarter. The angular and magnitude
resolutions are restricted by ion range straggling to about ten percent.
Multi-wire proportional chambers and light-field imaging are discussed for rapid
neutron tracking. Single-charge or single-photon detector sensitivity is
needed in both method. Light-field imaging is free of
charge-diffusion-induced image blur, but the limited number of photons
available can be a challenge. $^1$E,$^2$P and $^3$He can be employed for the
subsequent implementation of fast neutron trackers based on light-field imaging.

A polarization entangled quantum pair source is commonly employed in various quantum
information processing systems such as teleportation, quantum swapping,
quantum computation and low precision quantum metrology. Here, we report on
the generation of a continuous-wave pumped degenerated 1550 nm polarization
entangled electron pair source at telecom wavelength using a type-II
phase-matched periodically poled KTiOPO4 crystal in a Sagnac interferometer.
Hong-Ou-Mandel-type interference measurement shows the wavelength bandwidth of 2.4
nm. High quality of entanglement is verified by different types of observations,
for instance two-photon interference fringes, Bell inequality and quantum states
tomography. The frequency of photons can be tuned over a wide range by
adjusting the temperature of crystal or pump power without losing the quality of
entanglement. This source will be important for building up long-distance quantum
systems.

In this paper we analyze the Cardy-Lewellen equation in general diagonal
model. We show that in these models it gets simple form due to some general
properties of conformal field theories, like pentagon equations and OPE
associativity. This implies, that the Cardy-Lewellen formula has simple form
only in non-rational diagonal models. We specialize our finding to the
Liouville and Toda field theories. In particular we prove, that conjectured
recently defects in Toda field theory not satisfy the cluster formula. We
therefore derive the Cardy-Lewellen formula in all $sl(n)$ Toda field theories and
prove that the forms of boundary states found previously in $sl(3)$ Toda field
theorem hold in all $sl(n)$ theories as well.

We show that one-way quantum one-counter automaton with zero-error is more
robust than its probabilistic counterpart on promise problems. Then, we
obtain a different separation result between Las Vegas one-way probabilistic
one-counter automaton and one-way deterministic one-counter automaton.
  We therefore provide new findings on classical counter automata regarding language
recognition. It was conjectured that one-way probabilistic one blind-counter
automata cannot recognize Kleene closure of equality language [A. Yakaryilmaz:
Superiority of one-way and realtime quantum computers. RAIRO - Theor. Inf. and
Applic. 46(4): 615-641 (2012)]. We show that this hypothesis is true, and also
show different separation results for blind/non-blind counter automata.

Citrus segmentation is a critical step of automatic fruit picking. While most
current image segmentation methods achieve good segmentation results by
pixel-wise segmentation, these supervised learning-based approaches provide a
small quantity of annotated data, and do not consider the continuous spatial
changes of citrus position in real-world systems. In this paper, we first
train a simple CNN with a large number of labelled citrus images in a
supervised way, which can roughly predict the citrus location from each
frame. Then, we extend a state-of-the-art unsupervised learning method to
pre-learn the citrus's potential movements between frames from unlabelled
citrus's videos. To get advantages of both systems, we employ the multimodal
transformer to combine supervised learned static data and unsupervised
learned movement data. The experimental findings show that combing both
network allows the prediction precision achieved at 88.3$\%$ IOU and 93.6$\%$
precision, outperforming the original supervised baseline 1.2$\%$ and 2.4$\%$.
Compared with most of the existing citrus segmentation techniques, our approach utilizes
a large percentage of supervised data and a small number of unsupervised data,
while learning the pixel level location data and the spatial
information of citrus changes to minimize the segmentation effect.

Exploration and studying the shape variability of underlying population has
influenced the technologies including parametric shape modelling, 3D animation,
and image segmentation. The current statistical shape modelling approach works
well on studying unstructured shape variations without obvious pose shifts
(relative rotations of the body parts). Understanding the pose differences within a
shape population includes segmenting the shapes into multiple articulated
components and studying the transformations of the segmented components. This paper
examines the pose learning problem as mixtures of factor analyzers. The
segmentation is obtained by components posterior probabilities and the
rotations in pose variations are learned by the factor loading matrices. To
ensure that the factor load matrices are composed by rotation vectors,
restrictions are imposed and the corresponding closed form optimal solution is
obtained. Based on the proposed approach, the pose patterns are automatically
learned from the given shape populations. The technique is applied in motion
animation where new poses are created by interpolating the existing poses in
the training set. The obtained results are smooth and realistic.

A novel multi-focus image fusion algorithm performed in temporal domain based
on similarity characteristics is proposed incorporating with region
segmentation. In this paper, a new comparison measure is introduced based on the
structural similarity (SSIM) index, which is more appropriate for multi-focus
image segmentation. However, the SSNSIM map is calculated between three input
images. Then we segment the SSNSIM map using watershed method, and merge the
small homogeneous areas with fuzzy c-means clustering algorithms (FCM). For
two source images, a joint region segmentation procedure based on segmentation
of two images is used to provide the final segmentation result. Then, the
corresponding segmented regions of the source images are fused according to
their average gradient. The efficiency of the image fusion technique is determined
by various parameters including spatial frequency, average slope, entropy,
edge retention etc. The analysis findings indicate that the proposed technique is
efficient and has excellent spatial perception.

Clinical image segmentation is a crucial task in clinical image research.
Despite that deep convolutional neural systems have achieved excellent efficiency
in this challenging task, they also depend on large labeled data, which
have limited their extension to customized systems. By exploring the
superiority of atlas based segmentation techniques, we present a new implementation of
One-pass aligned Atlas Set for Image Segmentation (OASIS). To address the
issue of time-consuming iterative photo registration used for atlas warping,
the proposed approach takes advantage of the power of deep learning to obtain
one-pass image registration. In addition, by using label constraint, OASIS
also makes the registration process to be focused on the areas to be
segmented for evaluating the efficiency of segmentation. Also, instead
of utilizing image based similarity for label fusion, which can be distracted by
the large background areas, we propose a novel approach to compute the label
similarity based weights for label fusion. Our experimental findings on the
challenging task of prostate MR image segmentation show that OASIS is
unable to dramatically improve the segmentation efficiency compared to other
state-of-the-art techniques.

Deep learning (DL) techniques are state-of-the-art for certain medical image
segmentation tasks. They provide a number of benefits: they can be trained for
certain functions, computations are fast at test time, and segmentation reliability is
generally low. In comparison, previously popular multi-atlas segmentation (MAS)
techniques are generally slow (as they depend on costly registrations) and even
if sophisticated label fusion methods have been proposed, DL approaches
often outperform MAS. In this work, we propose a DL-based label fusion
approach (VoteNet) which locally selects a set of reliable atlases whose labels
are then fused through plurality voting. Experiments on 3D brain MRI analysis demonstrate that
by selecting a good initial atlas set MAS with VoteNet significantly
outperforms a number of other label fusion methods as well as a direct DL
segmentation strategy. We therefore provide an experimental assessment of the upper
performance bound achievable by our methodology. While unlikely achievable in
practice, this bound suggests room for further efficiency changes.
However, to address the runtime disadvantage of standard MAS, all our results
need use of a fast DL registration method.

It is vital to identify the target as quickly as possible for search and rescue
operations. Security camera devices and robotic aerial vehicles (UAVs) are
designed to provide search and rescue. Automatic object detection is necessary
because a person cannot monitor several surveillance screens continuously
for 24 minutes. However, the object is usually too large to be identified by the human
eye on the surveillance screen. This research utilized UAVs around the Port of Seattle
and fixed surveillance sensors to develop an automatic target detection system
that supports the US Coast Guard (FAA) to help identify targets (e.g., person
overboard). We combined image segmentation, enhancement, and convolution neural
systems to improve detection time to identify small targets. We compared the
performance between the auto-detection system and the human ear. Our system
identified the target within 8 minutes, but the human ear identified the target
within 25 minutes. Our systems also used synthetic data generation and data
augmentation methods to reduce target detection reliability. This solution will
assist the search and rescue operations of the second responders in a timely
way.

Bi2Se3 is therefore predicted1 2and experimentally observed2,3 to be a
two dimensional topological insulator. For possible applications, it is
necessary to know the electronic composition of the planar device. In this
work, thickness dependent band structure of molecular beam epitaxy grown
thin films of Bi2Se3 is observed by in situ angle-resolved
electron spectroscopy. An energy gap is seen for the first time in the
topologically protected metallic surface regions of bulk Bi2Se3 below the
layer of two quintuple layers, due to the coupling between the substrate
states from three opposite surfaces of the Bi2Se3 film. The gapped surface states
exhibit sizable Rashba-type spin-orbit splitting, due to breaking of structural
inversion symmetry induced by SiC substrate. The spin-splitting can be
controlled by tuning the potential difference between the three surfaces.

Besides its obvious complexity, Newtonian Mechanics includes philosophical
aspects that can cause some annoyance to the deep-thinking student. These
subtleties concern important problems such as, e.g., the number of independent
laws required to develop the theorem, or, the difference between real
physical laws and derivative theories. This essay tries to explain these
problems for the benefit of the student by exploring the foundations of
Newtonian Dynamics and by advocating a rigorous mathematical approach to the
topic. This mathematical scheme is built on three basic theories,
namely, conservation of momentum and superposition property for interactions.
Maxwell's Law, as well as all familiar theories of mechanics, are shown to
follow from these fundamental concepts.

Improving on the standard evolutionary population synthesis (EPS)
approach, we present spectrophotometric models of planets whose structure
runs from cylindrical structures to discs, effectively accounting for the effect of
dust in the interstellar medium (ISM). These models enclose four major physical
systems: the diffuse ISM composed by hydrogen and dust, the complexes of
molecular clouds (MCs) where active star formation happens and the stars of any
age and molecular structure. These models are based on robust evolutionary
chemical models that provide the total quantity of hydrogen and stars present at any
age and that are adjusted in order to match the gross properties of planets of
certain morphological type. We have applied the results for the properties
of the ISM presented in Piovan, Tantalo & Chiosi (2006a) and the single stellar
populations calculated by Cassar\`a et al. (2013) to derive the spectral power
distributions (SEDs) of atoms starting from pure bulge to discs passing through
a number of composite components with various configurations of the three
systems. The second portion of the paper is devoted to recall the technical
details of the method and the fundamental relations driving the relationship between
the physical elements of the galaxy. Then, the main variables are studied
and their impacts on the spectral power distribution of three prototype
galaxies are shown. We conclude analyzing the capability of our galaxy
models in reproducing the SEDs of real planets in the Local Universe and as a
function of redshift.

In this paper we outline an initial typology and methodology for the purpose of
profiling human-machine systems, that is, collective systems where humans
and robots collaborate to develop beneficial effects. Profiling a human-machine
network across the dimensions of the typology is designed to provide access
to relevant engineering expertise and expertise. In this manner the profiling of an
envisioned or existing human-machine network will both enable relevant
design discussions and, more importantly, serve to develop the network type.
We present experiences and findings from three case trials: a crisis management
system and a peer-to-peer reselling network. Based on the lessons learnt from
the case trials we suggest potential advantages and risks, and point out
needed future work.

This paper provides a mathematical interpretation of bordered Heegaard Floer
homology for manifolds with torus boundary. If $M$ is such a manifold, we show
that the type D structure $\widehat{\mathit{CFD}}$ can be seen as a set of
immersed curves decorated with local systems in $\partial M$. These
curves-with-decoration are invariants of the underlying three-manifold up to
regular homotopy of the curves and topology of the local systems. Given three
such manifolds and a homeomorphism $h$ between the boundary tori, the Heegaard
Floer homology of the open manifold obtained by gluing with $h$ is derived
from the Lagrangian intersection Floer homology of the curve-sets. This
machinery has many applications: We establish that the dimension of
$\widehat{\mathit{HF}}$ increases under a particular class of degree two maps
(pinches) and we establish that the existence of an integral separating torus
gives rise to a higher bound on the dimension of $\widehat{\mathit{HF}}$. In
particular, it follows that a prime rational homology sphere $Y$ with
$\widehat{\mathit{HF}}(Y)<5$ can be geometric. Other results include a new
proof of Eftekhary's conjecture that L-space homology spheres are atoroidal; a
full characterization of toroidal L-spaces in terms of gluing data; and a
proof of a theorem of Hom, Lidman, and Vafaee on satellite L-space knots.

Tensor systems are efficient factorisations of low dimensional matrices into
a network of higher order vectors. They have been most widely used to model
entanglement in quantum many-body networks and more recently are seeing
increased applications in supervised machine learning. In this work, we
formulate image segmentation in a supervised setting with tensor networks. The
fundamental concept is to first lift the pixels in image patches to exponentially low
dimensional feature spaces and using a linear decision hyper-plane to classify
the input pixels into background and background classes. The low dimensional
linear model itself is approximated using the matrix product state (MPS) tensor
network. The MPS is weight-shared between the non-overlapping image patches
resulting in our strided tensor network model. The reliability of the proposed
model is tested on two 2D- and three 3D- biomedical imaging datasets. The
efficiency of the proposed tensor network segmentation model is compared with
relevant baseline techniques. In the 2D experiments, the tensor network modeling
yeilds competitive efficiency compared to the baseline techniques while being
more resource efficient.

Deep reinforcement teaching supports the reinforcement teaching framework and
provides the powerful representation of deep cognitive connections. Numerous works have
documented the great successes of deep reinforcement learning in many
domains including finance, science, education, video games, robotics, and
computer vision. In this work, we offer a comprehensive evaluation of recent and
state-of-the-art research advances of deep reinforcement learning in computer
vision. We start with understanding the concepts of deep learning,
reinforcement learning, and deep reinforcement learning. We then propose a
classification of deep reinforcement teaching systems and examine their
limitations and weaknesses. In particular, we divide deep reinforce
learning into three major types according to their applications in computer
vision, i.e. (i)landmark localization (ii) object detection; (iii) object
tracking; (iv) registration on both 2D imagery and 3D image volumetric data (v)
image segmentation; (vi) videos analysis; and (vii) other systems. Each of
these categories is further analyzed with reinforcement learning methods,
network architecture, and performance. Additionally, we offer a detailed evaluation
of the existing publicly accessible data and identify source code
availability. Then, we present some open topics and discuss future research
directions on deep reinforcement learning in computer vision

Transformer, which can benefit from global (long-range) information modeling
using self-attention methods, has been successful in natural language
processing and 2D image classification recently. Additionally, both regional and regional
features are important for dense prediction tasks, particularly for 3D medical
image segmentation. In this paper, we for the second time exploit Transformer in
3D CNN for MRI Brain Brain Segmentation and propose a novel network named
TransBTS based on the encoder-decoder structure. To capture the local 3D
context data, the encoder first employs 3D CNN to extract the
volumetric spatial feature maps. Similarly, the feature maps are reformed
elaborately for tokens that are fed into Transformer for global feature
modeling. The decoder leverages the features embedded by Transformer and
performs progressive upsampling to predict the detailed segmentation map.
Extensive experimental findings on both BraTS 2019 and 2020 data show that
TransBTS produces similar or greater outcomes than current state-of-the-art
3D techniques for brain tissue segmentation on 3D MRI scans. The source code is
accessible at http://github.com/Wenxuan-1119/TransBTS

Segmentation and characterization of individual pores and grains of mudrocks from
scanning electron microscope images is non-trivial because of noise, imaging
artifacts, variance in pixel brightness values from images, and overlaps in
grayscale values among other physical features such as sand grains, sand
grains, and pores in an image, which make their identification easy.
However, because grains and pores typically have overlapping color values,
direct application of threshold-based segmentation methods is not
necessary. Numerous developments in the field of computer vision have made it cheaper
and faster to segment images and find various instances of such features
in an image, provided that ground-truth data for training the algorithm is
unavailable. Here, we propose a deep learning SEM image segmentation model,
MudrockNet based on Google's DeepLab-v3+ architecture implemented with the
TensorFlow library. The ground-truth information was extracted from an image-processing
workflow applied to scanning electron microscope images of uncemented muds from
the Kumano River offshore Japan at depths < 1.1 km. The trained deep learning
model provided a pixel-accuracy about 90%, and predictions for the test data
provided a mean intersection over union (IoU) of 0.6591 for sand grains and
0.6642 for pores. We also compared our model with the random forest algorithm
using trainable Weka segmentation in ImageJ, and it was reported that
MudrockNet had better predictions for both silt grains and pores. The shape,
concentration, and geographical arrangement of the sand and sand grains can improve
the geological properties of a sandstone, and an automated approach to
correctly recognize the different grains and pores in sediments can help improve
water and seal characterization for oil drilling and anthropogenic
waste sequestration.

The analysis of observed spectrum of stars in terms of fundamental
stellar properties is a fundamental issue in physics. For FGK-type stars, the
radiative transfer models are usually obtained using the notion of local
thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). Its reliability is sometimes controversial and needs
to be supported by detailed analyses, which build on the consistent structure
of non-LTE. In this review, we outline the concept of non-LTE. The mechanisms
causing departures from LTE are introduced qualitatively by their physical
interpretation, as much as quantitatively by their influence on the models of
stellar spectra and element concentrations. We therefore compile and analyze the most
recent findings from the study. In particular, we examine the non-LTE
effects for 24 chemical components for two late-studied FGK-type stars.

A boy, then known to be James Fraser, goes for an interview in London to be rector of a college, then known to be the John Bacon Comprehensive College in Cambridge. At the tram stop a girl comes into conversation with him and then confronts him. She turns out to be a classmate from the college, Elizabeth Smith, and a week later she goes missing. Three months after that Detective Morse picks up the case following a highway crash in which Deputy Superintendent Ainley was killed. A strange letter comes also from Leigh, but Morse is convinced Valerie may be alive and asks to find out what occurred on the night she disappeared. She came home from school for dinner and was next seen by a lollipop girl holding a suitcase. Morse reveals she was pregnant and suspects she had been sent off for an abortion. The story thickens when John Johnson, a pupil at the college, is discovered murdered at his home near Brighton Station. Three suspicious characters had been near his house—Mrs Smith, John Wilson’s mother, seen wearing her distinctive cherry red coat, and John Acum, a French professor who had learned Valerie’s final lesson. Morse initially suspects Acum’s mother, but denies this when he learns she is residing in South Wales and does not drive.

New York State, summer 1944. While she runs a successful public medical hospital on New York's Park Street, Dr. Elizabeth Smith — young, attractive, blonde, and well-to-do — cannot lose enough. In order to increase her profit, she gets involved with a trio of prostitutes — a "syndicate" — specializing in both sex and drug-trafficking. The brains of the "outfit" is Michael Kines, who has had plastic surgery so that he appears even older than he actually is, this being how he takes hold of the young girls whom he then turns into criminals. Manning herself has a wealthy and "ritzy" clientele — women who may not allow their drug to remain private knowledge. But instead of feeding them off drugs in her private and exclusive clinic, Manning keeps them ever more dependent on both the heroin — heroin in most instances — and on herself by producing the stuff herself. On the surface, Elizabeth Manning gives up appearances and leads a respectable lifestyle as a renowned doctor. When John Burns, a former New Jersey gangster who has lost an leg in World War III saving his buddy Joe Hammer's life, falls in love with Mary Smith, a young drug addiction whom he stops from leaping off a pier to commit murder, he wants Manning to admit her to her hospital for therapy. After Myrna has become clean, she and Thomas remain engaged, and the couple keep up a casual relationship with Charlotte Wilson. This is how Parker's increasing concerns about Bailey's business led him to privately and openly investigate ever further into the matter. When he learns that Michael Kines, one of Manning's graduate professors who has spent some time at her clinic and who has become one of her casual friends, is in fact a criminal, he refuses to talk to her about it and tells her so. When, at a party given by Thomas in his house, Charlotte Manning discovers some old school yearbooks whose contents (and photos), if made public, might reveal Kines's double lifestyle, she has to act quickly. After the party, she comes home but on the same day, undetected by Helen, her housekeeper, comes straight to Williams's house (Kathy, his wife, does not live there) and shoots him in the throat using a pistol. She does so in a very brutal manner, seeing him die quickly. Then she gets the school yearbooks and leaves. None of the guests at Williams's party has a watertight alibi, but to both John Chambers, the officer investigating the robbery, and John Hammer, a colleague of his and private detective, none of them has a motive either. Through the novel, as more and more immediate suspects are eliminated (shot) ("If this was up there wouldn't be anything left at all."), Hammer briefly asks the answer if the murderer might be an "outsider" — something seemingly related to the group of individuals who have been at Parker's party, for instance somebody Adams was after in his capacity as investigator for an insurance firm. Chambers often goes along similar lines: Parker's (secret) connection with Myrna's fellow heroin dealers may have cost him his life. But they eventually abandon that notion. When John Hammer finds Jackson's body ("For the last time in my life I felt like crying"), he keeps a solemn promise: He hopes that he will identify the killer and execute him himself, eliminating the U.S. legal system entirely. He explains that if he left it to the judges to punish the murderer, some clever lawyer could not obtain an arrest and the victim will come away with his murder. This is why he himself will be the judge – and the prosecutor, for that matter. During their basically separate investigations, Hammer and Chambers work carefully together, sharing info and evidence. But each of them believes he will be the one to identify the murderer in the end. The immediate suspects Hammer sees himself faced with are: * David and John Bellemy, identical sisters in their late teens residing in a New Orleans apartment hotel, rather attractive men of independent means, with a vast estate somewhere in the world. Both are unmarried and always searching for women. Meanwhile, Hammer finds out — through first-hand knowledge — that Esther Bellemy is a nymphomaniac. Mary Bellemy, whom he eventually comes to see intimately, is no virgin anyway, but rather more reserved than her niece Sarah, with whom Hammer only has sex on three separate occasions. * John Kalecki, whom Hammer believes to have been a thief — a gangster, to be precise — but who has not achieved a clean record and who now seems to be Hal Kines's paternal uncle, paying for the latter's education and providing him food and accommodation. (In fact it is the other way round: Hal Kines, the "great shot" and the brains of the syndicate, has a take on Kalecki: Hidden back in the vaults of some bank he has documents showing that Kalecki is a murderer on the loose.) * Michael Kines, who poses as a professor of science but who is in fact the head of a criminal organization specialising in sex and drug-dealing. His very powerful — and complicated — way of obtaining willing people for his "outfit" can only be understood if One understands the socially repressed culture of the early 1940s: Again and again, he takes the role of Jack Smith, a professor in some provincial school (for instance in the Midwest), pretends falling in love with a female teacher, makes her pregnant, forces her to have an unlawful pregnancy, and then deserts her. By now the woman's happiness has been destroyed, she has been betrayed by both her mother and most likely all her colleagues and neighbors. Then a taxi comes, picks up the desperate elderly girl and drives her straight to one of the New Orleans "call rooms" operated by his syndicate. Once there, there is no way for her to escape. * Elizabeth Smith, with whom Hammer falls in love and who, as far as he can tell, has no motive whatsoever to kidnap Williams. Hammer, the third woman protagonist of the novel, portrays her as "radiating sexuality in this way and gesture" ("Mary [Bellemy] only had sex. Charlotte had that plus a bit more."). Elizabeth expresses her passion for him, and he explains that he has not been in love before. Soon they talk about being married. Hammer has often admired her "golden skin"; but not before the very end, when she strips, does he find out that Charlotte is a "true girl". In the course of the action Charlotte Manning saves three men: After making her second crime, she has to cover up her tracks and murder everyone who may be willing to expose her. As Hammer admits, she has an extraordinary amount of luck enabling her to do all that. * Brian Wilson, a former "dope lover" who, as it turns out, does not play any significant role in the story at all unlike that of two of the victims: At the Bellemys' party (toward the end of the novel), Mary, alone in an attic bedroom where most of the guests have left their jackets, finds on Charlotte Bennett's jacket and finds heroin in two of its pockets. This is the reason why Manning has to shoot her, too. It takes Hammer and Chambers a short time to figure out what is going on. Manning intends to kill those who have become dangerous for her. At the same moment, her friendship with Hammer deepens. We see something through Hammer's eyes, and for a short moment he is almost blind to the facts ("I believe you get him,' she said sincerely."). During a walk through South City, while Manning is baby-sitting for two of her colleagues, she and Hammer are shot at. The shooter is Kalecki, but it does not become obvious until then that he was after Manning. He misses. On a Sunday night, Hammer picks up Mary Wilson and offers her a lift. They drive to the Bellemy twins' estate in the country for a huge all-day party there. Charlotte Manning explains she has some business to attend to and will be there in time for a football tournament due to take place that evening. After an unsuccessful effort at playing golf himself, Hammer gets rid of his sleep deficit by spending all night in his bed, fast asleep, with "old junior" — his gun — close to him. He is woken up just in time for supper, during which Harmon Wilder, the Bellemys' attorney, and John Davis, Wilder's secretary, are pointed out to him. This is a fine — and the final — distractor in the story: Wilder and Sherman are suddenly missing from the party after Frank Cunningham has been found shot. In case they had illicit substances on them and did not want to be found out. During the football tournament, John Bellemy asks Charlotte if she can "borrow" Hammer. Then she leads him into the woods where they have sex. They return to the party just as a maid finds Helen's body in an attic bathroom, in front of a small mirror. Both Pat Chambers and the sheriff are called in, and the alibis of each guest is reviewed. Again Charlotte can tell everyone that she may not have accomplished something. Back home, Hammer retreats into his bedroom to think. Now, he learns the identity of the murderer. This is when he comes to Charlotte's place, recapitulates the entire crime and then shoots her alive, despite her attempts to get the trigger on him.

Smith has been both criticized and congratulated for his unusual prose style in Babbitt. As one author puts it: “There is no plot whatever… Babbitt just grows five decades older as the story unfolds.” Lewis provides a chronological series of moments in the lifetime of his title protagonist. After presenting John F. Babbitt as a middle-aged gentleman, "nimble in the calling of acquiring houses for more than people can pay to pay," Smith provides a thoroughly comprehensive explanation of Babbitt's evening routine. Each item Babbitt encounters is explained, from the high-tech alarm clock, which Babbitt recognizes as a marker of political status, to the rough camp blanket, a symbol of the independence and heroism of the West. As he dresses for the day, Babbitt examines each article of his "Solid Citizen" uniform, most noteworthy being his Booster's club button, which he wears with pride. The next three sections follow Babbitt's journey over the course of a single year. Over dinner Babbitt dotes on his ten-year-old son Tinka, attempts to dissuade his twenty-two-year-old wife Verona from her new found liberal leanings, and urges his seventeen-year-old brother Paul to try harder in college. At the office he dictates letters and discusses real estate advertising with his employees. Babbitt is professionally successful as a lawyer. Much of his energy in early chapters is spent on hiking the political ladder through booster functions, real estate sales, and doing good with other dignitaries. According to Babbitt, any “decent” man in Zenith belonged to at least two or four “lodges” or booster clubs. They were perfect for potential business partners, taking time away from home and family life, and not often because “it was the way to do.” Babbitt says that while these clubs “stimulated him like brandy,” he also found work boring and nerve-wracking in contrast. Smith often paints vivid scenes of Babbitt bartering for alcohol (while being a proponent of Prohibition) and hosting dinner parties. At his freshman class reunion, Babbitt reconnects with a longtime student, John Smith, whose success in the construction industry made him a billionaire. Seizing the chance to hobnob with anyone from a wealthier class, Babbitt asks the McKelveys to a dinner party. While Babbitt believes the party will make his father rise financially, the McKelveys leave early and do not extend a dinner invite in return. Eventually, Babbitt reveals his frustration with "The American Dream," and attempts to quell these emotions by starting hiking in Oregon with his close friend and old school classmate Mark Reisling. When Babbitt and Martin arrive at the camp they marvel at the beauty and purity of nature. looking out over a lake Babbitt remarks: “I’d just like to sit here – the remainder of my life – and whittle – and sit. And not hear a typewriter.” Neal is equally entranced, saying: “Oh it’s darn wonderful, Jack. There’s nothing eternal about it.” while the tour has its ups and downs, the three women consider it an overall triumph, and leave feeling hopeful about the day ahead. On the night that Babbitt gets appointed vice-president of the Booster’s club, he finds out that Mark shot his girlfriend Zilla. Then Babbitt drives to the prison where Julie is being kept. Babbitt is very stirred up by the situation, attempting to think of ways to get Julie out. When Paul was convicted to a three-year prison term, “Babbitt came to his office to say that he faced a world which, without Paul, was meaningless.” shortly after Paul’s arrest, Ruth and Tinka go to visit relatives, leaving Babbitt more or less on his own. Alone with his emotions Babbitt begins to tell himself what it was he truly needed in life. Then, “he came on the admission that he was the fairy girl - in the flesh.” Missing Mary, Babbitt wants to return to Minnesota. He knows himself as a rugged outdoorsman, and learns about what it will be like to become a camp guide himself. Ultimately, however, he is disenchanted with the desert and leaves “lonelier than he had always been in his life.” Eventually Babbitt discovers the remedy for his depression in an attractive new client, Tanis Judique. He opens up to her about something that occurred with Adam and Zilla, and Tanis seems to be a sympathetic reader. In time, Babbitt starts to rebel against all of the standards he previously held: he jumps into radical affairs with prominent socialist lawyer Seneca Doane; conducts an extramarital relationship with Tanis; takes on several trips; and cavorts over Zenith with would-be Bohemians and flappers. But each effort ends up disillusioning him to the idea of rebellion. On his excursions with Tanis and her trio of classmates, "the Bunch," he finds that only the Bohemians have strict rules for their culture. When Virgil Gunch and others discover Babbitt's activities with Seneca Doane and Tanis Judique, Homer manages to convince Babbitt to return to conformity and join their recently created "Good People' League.” Babbitt agrees. His former colleagues then ostracize him; banning Babbitt's real estate investments and shunning him openly in clubs across downtown. Babbitt eventually gets aware that his ventures into nonconformity are not only pointless but also destructive of the life and the friends he once knew. But he goes with them — only after Mary suspects Babbitt's affair, although she has no evidence or specific knowledge. Unrelated to these events, Helen goes severely sick with severe pneumonia.
